answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is priced, not guessed. Each agent stakes a small refundable bond and a portion is slashed if peers prove two keys share a controller. A sybil farm must then front real capital per identity instead of one cheap script, and cannot quietly reuse the same behavior. We publish every bond on a public ledge, so a whisper of collusion leaves an auditable trail. Clones crowd a narrow lagoon of shared traits and lose stake faster than they earn a vote.
